If a bhikkhunī should travel within the kingdom in an area designated as suspicious and dangerous without a caravan, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Tiroraṭṭha Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should travel in another kingdom in an area designated as suspicious and dangerous without a caravan, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Antovassa Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should go on a journey during the Rains, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Cārikanapakkamana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī, having completed the Rains-residence, should not set out on a journey even for as little as five or six yojanas, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Cittāgāravagga

## Rājāgāra Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should go to see a king's palace, or a picture gallery, or a monastery, or a park, or a lotus pond, she commits a pācittiya offence.
91:
## Āsandiparibhuñjana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should use a couch or a chair with legs exceeding eight finger-breadths, or a throne with figures of wild beasts such as lions, tigers, or leopards, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Suttakantana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should spin thread, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Gihiveyyāvacca Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should perform services for laypeople, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Adhikaraṇa Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī, being spoken to by another bhikkhunī thus: "Lady, come, settle this legal issue," should agree by saying "Very well," and later, when there is no obstacle, should neither settle it herself nor make an effort to have it settled, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Bhojanadāna Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should with her own hand give food or edibles to a layperson, or to a male wanderer, or to a female wanderer, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Āvasathacīvara Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should use a communal robe (rest-house robe) without having relinquished it, she commits a pācittiya offence.
92:
## Āvasathavihāra Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should set out on a journey without having handed over the dwelling (with a door-leaf) to someone to look after, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Tiracchānavijjāpariyāpuṇana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should learn worldly arts (tiracchānavijjā) which are contrary to the path to heaven and Nibbāna, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Tiracchānavijjāvācana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should teach worldly arts, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Ārāmavagga
Chapter on the Monastery.

## Ārāmapavisana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī, knowing that a monastery contains monks, should enter without asking permission, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Bhikkhu-akkosana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should scold or revile a monk, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Gaṇaparibhāsana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī, being angry, should revile a group, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Pavārita Sikkhāpada
93:
If a bhikkhunī, having been invited or having already refused further food, should eat or consume food or edibles, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Kulamaccharinī Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should be stingy regarding families, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Abhikkhukāvāsa Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should spend the Rains-residence in a dwelling where there are no monks, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Apavāraṇā Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī, having completed the Rains-residence, should not perform Pavāraṇā before both Saṅghas (the Bhikkhu Saṅgha and the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha) in respect of three matters: what has been seen, heard, or suspected, she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Ovāda Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī should not go for the sake of receiving exhortation or for the sake of the communal acts (such as Uposatha and Pavāraṇā), she commits a pācittiya offence.

## Ovādūpasaṅkamana Sikkhāpada
Every fortnight, a bhikkhunī should expect two things from the Bhikkhu Saṅgha: the asking of the date of the Uposatha and the approaching for exhortation. For a bhikkhunī who lets that fortnight pass, she commits a pācittiya offence.
94:
## Pasākhejāta Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should have a boil or a wound that has arisen in the groin (the area between the thighs or below the navel) lanced, or cut, or washed, or smeared with medicine, or bandaged, or unbandaged by a man, one-on-one, without having informed the Saṅgha or a group, it is an offense of expiation.

## Gabbhinī Vagga

## Gabbhinī Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a pregnant woman, it is an offense of expiation.

## Pāyantī Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a nursing woman, it is an offense of expiation.

## First Sikkhamānā Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a trainee (sikkhamānā) who has not trained for two years in the six rules, it is an offense of expiation.

## Second Sikkhamānā Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a trainee who has trained for two years in the six rules but has not received formal agreement (vuṭṭhāna-sammuti) from the Saṅgha, it is an offense of expiation.
95:

Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a woman who has lived with a husband (a married woman) but is less than twelve years old, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Second Gihigata Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a woman who has lived with a husband and is twelve years old, but has not trained for two years in the six rules, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Third Gihigata Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a woman who has lived with a husband and is twelve years old, and has trained for two years in the six rules, but has not received formal agreement (vuṭṭhāna-sammuti) from the Saṅgha, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

Whatever bhikkhunī, having ordained a companion (sahajīvinī), should neither support her nor have her supported for two years, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Pavattinīnānubandhana Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should not follow her preceptor (pavattinī) who ordained her for two years (to perform duties and services), for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Second Sahajīvinī Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī, having ordained a companion, should neither take her along nor have her taken along to a place at least five or six yojanas away, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Kumāribhūta Vagga

## First Kumāribhūta Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a maiden (kumāribhūta) who is less than twenty years old, it is an offense of expiation.

## Second Kumāribhūta Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a maiden who is twenty years old, but has not trained for two years in the six rules, it is an offense of expiation.

## Third Kumāribhūta Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a maiden who is twenty years old, and has trained for two years in the six rules, but has not received formal agreement (vuṭṭhāna-sammuti) from the Saṅgha, it is an offense of expiation.

## Ūnadvādasavassa Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain others when she herself has been ordained for less than twelve years, it is an offense of expiation.

## Paripuṇṇadvādasavassa Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī, though she has been ordained for twelve years, should ordain others without having received formal agreement (vuṭṭhāpana-sammuti) from the Saṅgha, it is an offense of expiation.

## Khiyyanadhamma Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī, being told, "Noble lady, it is not yet suitable for you to ordain [others]," should agree, saying, "Very well," and should afterwards engage in criticism and disparagement, it is an offense of expiation.
97:
## First Sikkhamānanavuṭṭhāpana Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī, having said to a trainee (sikkhamānā), "Noble lady, if you give me a robe, I will ordain you," should afterwards, when there is no obstacle, neither ordain her nor make an effort to have her ordained, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Second Sikkhamānanavuṭṭhāpana Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī, having said to a trainee, "Noble lady, if you follow me for two years, I will ordain you," should afterwards, when there is no obstacle, neither ordain her nor make an effort to have her ordained, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Sokāvāsa Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a trainee who associates with men, who associates with young men, who is ill-tempered, and who causes grief (or is a source of grief), for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Ananuññāta Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a trainee who has not been permitted by her parents or by her husband, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Pārivāsika Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain a trainee by giving consent while undergoing a probationary period (pārivāsika), for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.
98:
## Anuvassa Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain [someone] every year, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Ekavassa Sikkhāpada
Whatever bhikkhunī should ordain two [persons] in a single year, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

Whatever bhikkhunī, not being ill, should carry a sunshade and wear sandals, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

Whatever bhikkhunī, not being ill, should travel in a vehicle, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

Whatever bhikkhunī should wear a hip-ornament (girdle), for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

Whatever bhikkhunī should wear women's ornaments, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

Whatever bhikkhunī should bathe with scented water or cosmetic coloring, for that bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation.

## Vāsitaka Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī bathes with scented sesame powder, she commits an offence of expiation (pācittiya).

If a bhikkhunī has another bhikkhunī rub or massage her body, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Sikkhamāna-ummaddāpana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī has a sikkhamāna rub or massage her body, she commits an offence of expiation.

If a bhikkhunī has a sāmaṇerī rub or massage her body, she commits an offence of expiation.

If a bhikkhunī has a laywoman rub or massage her body, she commits an offence of expiation.

If a bhikkhunī sits on a seat in front of a bhikkhu without asking permission, she commits an offence of expiation.

If a bhikkhunī asks a question to a bhikkhu who has not given permission to be questioned, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Asaṅkaccika Sikkhāpada

## Dhamma-desanā Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī teaches the Dhamma to a man for more than five or six sentences without a wise woman present, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Bhūtārocana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī tells one who is not ordained about her own true attainment of superhuman states (jhāna, magga, or phala), she commits an offence of expiation.

## Duṭṭhullārocana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī tells one who is not ordained about another bhikkhunī's grave offence without the authorization of the bhikkhunīs, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Pathavīkhaṇana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī digs the earth or has it dug, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Musāvāda Vagga, the Tenth.
The Tenth Chapter on Lying is finished.

## Bhūtagāma Sikkhāpada
In destroying vegetation (trees and grass), there is an offence of expiation.

## Aññavādaka Sikkhāpada
In prevarication (evasive speech) and in causing annoyance, there is an offence of expiation.

## Ujjhāpanaka Sikkhāpada
In disparaging and complaining, there is an offence of expiation.
102:
## Paṭhama Senāsana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī, having spread or having had spread in the open air a bed, a chair, a mat, or a stool belonging to the Saṅgha, departs without putting it away or having it put away, or without asking permission, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Dutiya Senāsana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī, having spread or having had spread bedding in a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, departs without putting it away or having it put away, or without asking permission, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Anupakhajja Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī, in a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, knowingly encroaches upon a bhikkhunī who arrived first and makes her bed there, thinking, "Whoever finds it cramped will depart," and doing it for this reason alone and no other, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Nikkaḍḍhana Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī, being angry and displeased, drives out or has another drive out a bhikkhunī from a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Vehāsakuṭi Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī, in a dwelling belonging to the Saṅgha, sits or lies down on a bed or a chair with detachable legs in an upper-story room, she commits an offence of expiation.
103:
## Mahallakavihāra Sikkhāpada
When a bhikkhunī is having a large dwelling built, she may supervise the roofing for up to two or three layers, standing where there are no crops, until the door frames are fixed, the bolts are fitted, and the window openings are finished. If she supervises beyond that, even while standing where there are no crops, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Sappāṇaka Sikkhāpada
If a bhikkhunī knowingly pours or has someone pour water containing living beings onto grass or clay, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Bhūtagāma Vagga, the Eleventh.

## Āvasathapiṇဍa Sikkhāpada
A bhikkhunī who is not sick may eat one meal at a public rest-house. If she eats more than that, she commits an offence of expiation.

## Gaṇabhojana Sikkhāpada
Except on the right occasion, there is an offence of expiation in eating a group meal (gaṇabhojana). Here, these are the right occasions: the occasion of being sick, the occasion of giving robes, the occasion of making robes, the occasion of going on a journey, the occasion of embarking on a boat, a great occasion, and the occasion of a meal for ascetics. These are the right occasions.
104:
## Kāṇamātusikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī who has gone to a family is invited with cakes or meal-powder, she may accept two or three bowlfuls if she so desires. If she accepts more than that, it is a pācittiya offense. Having accepted two or three bowlfuls, she should take them away and share them with other bhikkhunīs; this is the proper practice in that case.

## Vikālabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī eats or consumes solid food or soft food at the wrong time (after noon), it is a pācittiya offense.

## Sannidhikārakasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī eats or consumes solid food or soft food that has been stored, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Dantaponasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī takes into her mouth food that has not been given, except for water and tooth-wood, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Uyyojanasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī says to another bhikkhunī, "Come, lady, let us enter the village or town for alms," and having had food given to her or not, sends her away, saying, "Go, lady, talking or sitting with you is not comfortable for me; talking or sitting alone is comfortable for me," if she does so for this reason alone and no other, it is a pācittiya offense.
105:
## Sabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī sits down, intruding, in a house where people are eating, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Rahopaṭicchannasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī sits with a man in a private, screened place, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Rahonisajjasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī sits one-on-one with a man in a private place, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Bhojanavaggo dvādasamo.

## Cārittasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī, being invited for a meal, without informing another bhikkhunī who is present, goes on a round among families before the meal or after the meal, except at the proper time, it is a pācittiya offense. In this case, the proper time is: the time of giving robes, the time of making robes; this is the proper time in that case.

## Mahānāmasikkhāpadaṃ
A bhikkhunī who is not sick may accept a four-month invitation for requisites, unless it is a renewed invitation or a permanent invitation. If she accepts beyond that, it is a pācittiya offense.
106:
## Uyyuttasenāsikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī goes to see an army on the march without a suitable reason, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Senāvāsasikkhāpadaṃ
If there is some reason for that bhikkhunī to go to the army, she may stay with the army for two or three nights. If she stays longer than that, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Uyyodhikasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī, while staying with the army for two or three nights, goes to a battlefield, or to a place of assembly, or to a battle array, or to see a review of the troops, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Surāpānasikkhāpadaṃ
In the drinking of fermented liquor or spirits, there is a pācittiya offense.

## Aṅgulipatodakasikkhāpadaṃ
In tickling with the fingers, there is a pācittiya offense.

## Hasadhammasikkhāpadaṃ
In playing in the water, there is a pācittiya offense.
107:
## Anādariyasikkhāpadaṃ
In disrespect, there is a pācittiya offense.

## Bhiṃsāpanasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī frightens a bhikkhunī, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Cārittavaggo terasamo.
The thirteenth chapter, the Chapter on Conduct, is finished.

## Jotisikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī, not being sick, desiring to warm herself, should kindle a fire or have one kindled without a suitable reason, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Nahānasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī bathes at intervals of less than half a month, except at the proper time, it is a pācittiya offense. In this case, the proper time is: "the remaining month and a half of the hot season" and "the first month of the rainy season"—these two and a half months are the time of heat, the time of fever, the time of sickness, the time of work, the time of going on a journey, the time of wind and rain; this is the proper time in that case.

## Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadaṃ
When a bhikkhunī obtains a new robe, she should apply one of the three methods of disfiguring its color: blue (or green), mud-color, or black. If a bhikkhunī, without applying one of the three...
108:
...methods of disfiguring its color, uses a new robe, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Vikappanasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī, having formally assigned a robe to a monk, or to a bhikkhunī, or to a female trainee (sikkhamānā), or to a novice (sāmaṇera), or to a female novice (sāmaṇerī), uses it without the assignment being rescinded, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Apanidhāpanasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī hides or causes to be hidden a bhikkhunī's bowl, or robe, or sitting cloth, or needle case, or belt, even if only in jest, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Sañciccasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī intentionally deprives a living being of life, it is a pācittiya offense.

## Sappāṇakasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī uses water knowing it to contain living beings (insects), it is a pācittiya offense.

## Ukkoṭanasikkhāpadaṃ
If a bhikkhunī, knowing that a legal issue has been settled according to the Dhamma, reopens it for further action, it is a pācittiya offense.
109:
## Training Rule on Traveling with a Caravan of Thieves
Should any bhikkhunī, by arrangement, travel along the same path with a caravan of thieves, even as far as the next village, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

## Training Rule on Ariṭṭha
Should any bhikkhunī say: "As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructions by the Blessed One are not able to cause an obstruction for one who indulges in them." That bhikkhunī should be told by the bhikkhunīs: "Lady, do not say such a thing. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One, for misrepresentation of the Blessed One is not good. The Blessed One would not say such a thing. Lady, in many ways the Blessed One has stated that obstructive things are indeed obstructions, and that they are able to cause an obstruction for one who indulges in them."

And if that bhikkhunī, though being spoken to by the bhikkhunīs, should still persist as before, that bhikkhunī should be exhorted by the bhikkhunīs up to three times for the relinquishing of that view. If, being exhorted up to three times, she relinquishes it, that is good. If she does not relinquish it, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

## The Fourteenth Chapter: Joti Vagga.
The fourteenth chapter, Joti Vagga, is finished.

## Training Rule on Associating with an Expelled Nun
Should any bhikkhunī, knowing that a bhikkhunī who speaks in such a way (holding a wrong view), who has not acted in accordance with the rule, and has not relinquished that view...
110:
(...should eat with her, live with her, or share a bed with her), it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

## Training Rule on Kaṇṭaka
If a female novice (samaṇuddesā) should also say: "As I understand the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One, those things called obstructions by the Blessed One are not able to cause an obstruction for one who indulges in them." That female novice should be told by the bhikkhunīs: "Lady novice, do not say such a thing. Do not misrepresent the Blessed One, for misrepresentation of the Blessed One is not good. The Blessed One would not say such a thing. Lady novice, in many ways the Blessed One has stated that obstructive things are indeed obstructions, and that they are able to cause an obstruction for one who indulges in them."

And if that female novice, though being spoken to by the bhikkhunīs, should still persist as before, that female novice should be told by the bhikkhunīs: "Lady novice, from this day forth, the Blessed One is no longer to be referred to as your teacher. And as for the right to share a bed with bhikkhunīs for two or three nights, which other female novices get, that too is no longer yours. Go away, you wretch, be gone!"

Should any bhikkhunī, knowing that a female novice has been thus expelled, entice her, or attend to her, or eat with her, or share a bed with her, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

## Training Rule on Legal Speaking
Should any bhikkhunī, when being spoken to by bhikkhunīs in accordance with the Dhamma, say: "Ladies, I will not...
111:
...train in this training rule until I have consulted another bhikkhunī who is wise and learned in the Vinaya," it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya). Monks, a bhikkhunī who is training should understand, should inquire, should investigate; this is the proper procedure in this case.

## Training Rule on Disparaging
Should any bhikkhunī, while the Pātimokkha is being recited, say: "What is the use of these minor and lesser training rules being recited? They only lead to remorse, distress, and confusion," it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for disparaging the training rules.

## Training Rule on Feigning Ignorance
Should any bhikkhunī, while the Pātimokkha is being recited every half-month, say: "Only now do I realize that this rule is included in the Suttas, is comprised in the Suttas, and comes up for recitation every half-month." If other bhikkhunīs know that this bhikkhunī has sat through the recitation of the Pātimokkha two or three times before, let alone more, that bhikkhunī is not released from the offense by feigning ignorance. Whatever offense she has committed therein, she should be dealt with according to the rule. Furthermore, a charge of feigning ignorance (moha) should be laid against her: "Lady, it is a loss for you, it is poorly gained by you, that you do not pay proper attention and take it to heart when the Pātimokkha is being recited." This is an offense of expiation (pācittiya) for feigning ignorance.
112:
## Training Rule on Striking
Should any bhikkhunī, being angry and displeased, give a blow to another bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

## Training Rule on Threatening
Should any bhikkhunī, being angry and displeased, raise a hand (as a weapon) against another bhikkhunī, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

## Training Rule on Groundless Accusation
Should any bhikkhunī harass another bhikkhunī with a groundless charge of an offense entailing a formal meeting of the Saṅgha (saṅghādisesa), it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

## Training Rule on Intentional Remorse
Should any bhikkhunī intentionally cause remorse to another bhikkhunī, thinking, "In this way, she will be uncomfortable even for a moment," if she does it for this reason alone and no other, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

## Training Rule on Eavesdropping
Should any bhikkhunī stand eavesdropping on bhikkhunīs who are engaged in a quarrel, a dispute, or a contention, thinking, "I will hear what they say," if she does it for this reason alone and no other, it is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).

## The Fifteenth Chapter: Diṭṭhi Vagga.
The fifteenth chapter, Diṭṭhi Vagga, is finished.
113:
## Kammapaṭibāhana Sikkhāpada
Whichever bhikkhunī, having given her consent to formal acts that are in accordance with the Dhamma, should later engage in criticism, it is an offence of Pācittiya.

## Chandaṃadatvāgamana Sikkhāpada
Whichever bhikkhunī, while a discussion for a decision is ongoing in the Saṅgha, should rise from her seat and depart without having given her consent, it is an offence of Pācittiya.

## Dubbala Sikkhāpada
Whichever bhikkhunī, having given a robe to the Saṅgha when it is in harmony, should later engage in criticism, saying: "The bhikkhunīs divert the Saṅgha's gains according to their acquaintances," it is an offence of Pācittiya.

## Pariṇāmana Sikkhāpada
Whichever bhikkhunī, knowing that a gain is intended for the Saṅgha, should divert it to an individual, it is an offence of Pācittiya.

## Ratana Sikkhāpada
Whichever bhikkhunī should pick up or have someone pick up a treasure or what is considered a treasure, except within a monastery or within a dwelling, it is an offence of Pācittiya. But if a bhikkhunī has picked up or had someone pick up a treasure or what is considered a treasure within a monastery or within a dwelling, it must be set aside, thinking: "Whoever it belongs to will take it." This is the proper course there.
114:
## Sūcighara Sikkhāpada
Whichever bhikkhunī should have a needle case made of bone, or of ivory, or of horn, it is an offence of Pācittiya involving breaking.

## Mañcapīṭha Sikkhāpada
When a bhikkhunī is having a new bed or chair made, it should be made with legs eight finger-breadths long according to the Sugata’s finger-breadth, excluding the lower frame. For one who exceeds that measure, it is an offence of Pācittiya involving cutting.

## Tūlonaddha Sikkhāpada
Whichever bhikkhunī should have a bed or chair made stuffed with cotton or down, it is an offence of Pācittiya involving pulling out.

## Kaṇḍuppaṭicchādi Sikkhāpada
When a bhikkhunī is having an itch-covering cloth made, it should be made according to the proper measure. Herein, this is the measure: four spans long according to the Sugata’s span, and two spans wide. For one who exceeds that measure, it is an offence of Pācittiya involving cutting.

## Nanda Sikkhāpada (The Training Rule on the Measure of the Sugata’s Robe)
Whichever bhikkhunī should have a robe made the size of the Sugata’s robe, or larger, it is an offence of Pācittiya involving cutting. Herein, this is the measure of the Sugata’s robe for the Sugata: nine spans long...
115:
...according to the Sugata’s span, and six spans wide. This is the measure of the Sugata’s robe for the Sugata.

## Dhammika Vagga, the Sixteenth.
Noble ladies, the one hundred and sixty-six Pācittiya rules have been recited. In respect of them, I ask the noble ladies: Are you pure in this? A second time I ask: Are you pure in this? A third time I ask: Are you pure in this? The noble ladies are pure in this; therefore they are silent. Thus do I record it.

## Ladies, these seven rules for the settlement of legal processes come up for recitation.

For the settlement and calming of legal processes (adhikaraṇa) as they arise: 

Verdict in the presence (Sammukhāvinaya) should be given.

Verdict of innocence (Sativinaya) should be given.

Verdict of past insanity (Amūḷhavinaya) should be given.

Decision by majority (Yebhuyyasikā) should be used.

Verdict of further misconduct (Tassapāpiyasikā) should be given.

Covering over as if with grass (Tiṇavatthāraka) should be used.
